title: Mood boards and references

body.text: Claude can analyze images — upload a reference and have it
decode why that work gives the feeling it does
: the color tone, fonts, layout, rhythm, white space — then turn that into words you can use with the team or client.

example: "Look at these 4 reference images, explain which elements make them feel 'premium minimal', then summarize it into a design direction"

title: From mood to something concrete

body.text: The classic problem: the client says 'I want it to feel bright but expensive' — have the AI
turn abstract words into a concrete spec
: a color range, a font style, examples of similar brands — to confirm you're on the same page before starting.

example: "Turn 'bright but expensive' into 3 directions, each with its color tone and mood, for the client to choose before we start designing"

question: What can Claude help with on reference images?

options.text: Decoding the elements that create the work's feeling
Stealing the work to use directly

question: When a client uses an abstract word like 'expensive-looking', what should you do?

options.text: Turn it into a concrete spec and confirm with the client first

question: What's the benefit of summarizing the design direction into words?

options.text: The team and client are on the same page before starting

question: To turn a mood into a design direction, what should you do?

options.text: Have the AI turn the mood into concrete things, like color, shape, tone

question: What is a mood board for?

options.text: Gathering inspiration to give a clear direction
